bib.title: GNNs as Predictors of Agentic Workflow Performances

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "GNNs as Predictors of Agentic Workflow Performances", Yuanshuo Zhang, Yuchen Hou, Bohan Tang, Shuo Chen, Muhan Zhang, Xiaowen Dong, Siheng Chen. arXiv 2503.11301v1, 14 Mar 2025. The text says "Preprint." and "position paper". I found no venue.

COVERAGE: I read the whole extraction, 60,794 of 60,794 chars, including the appendices (A.1 to D.2). I skimmed the reference list (about chars 44,000 to 50,000) for origins only. I did not read the notes, so fit is judged from the paper alone. Figure images were not inspected, only their captions and axis text.

CLAIMS
1. GNN predictors score well in-domain.
- number: average accuracy 0.7812 and average utility 0.7227 over 6 domains.
- setup: FLORA-Bench. GCN, GAT, GCNII, Graph Transformer and OFA each train and test inside one domain. 2-layer backbone, hidden dimension 512, Adam at 1e-4, 200 epochs, single RTX-4090. Labels are binary success or failure from GPT-4o-mini.
- quote: "all the GNN baselines demonstrate promising prediction accuracy and utility in most scenarios with an average accuracy of 0.7812 and an average utility of 0.7227 over 6 domains"
- where: Section 5.2, p.6.
- Per-domain accuracy averages (Table 2, p.7): Coding-GD 0.8443, Coding-AF 0.8296, Math-AF 0.7983, Reason-AF 0.8577, but Math-GD 0.6379 and Reason-GD 0.7224. Reason-GD utility is only 0.5980.
- The authors blame Math-GD and Reason-GD on few unique prompts (4 and 5) causing over-smoothing. That is a guess; they ran no ablation.

2. A GCN reward predictor speeds up workflow optimization about 125x with a small score loss.
- number: 125x faster, about 0.1 score loss, 0.11 gain over random rewards.
- setup: AFlow as the optimizer. A GCN predicts performance, and that prediction is the reward. Baselines are ground-truth rewards (real LLM runs) and random rewards. Tested on HumanEval, MMLU and MBPP. Table 8 averages: ground truth score 0.77, 2327 s, $2.28; random 0.56, 20 s, $0.01; GCN 0.67, 19 s, $0.01.
- quote: "GCN significantly accelerates refinement cycles by 125 times while the performance loss is 0.1 on average. GCN outperforms the 'random' baseline by 0.11 performance gain"
- where: Section 5.5, p.7. Table 8, p.15.
- Per benchmark, GCN against ground truth: HumanEval 0.89 against 0.92, MMLU 0.55 against 0.73, MBPP 0.56 against 0.67.
- 2327/19 is about 122x, so "125" is rounded.

3. Predictors fail to transfer across domains.
- number: cross-system accuracy mostly 0.48 to 0.68, and cross-task accuracy as low as 0.3256 (Table 5). Both are near or below chance for a binary label.
- setup: train on one domain, test on another. Cross-system means GD workflows to AF workflows, or the reverse, on the same task type. Cross-task means a different task type on the same system.
- quote: "GNNs demonstrate a significant decrease in the test domain compared with Table 2 and fail to predict accurately. This indicates that existing GNNs fail to generalize across domains."
- where: Section 5.4, p.7. Tables 3 and 5, pp.7-8.
- Example: Math-AF-GD GCN accuracy 0.4964.

4. Accuracy holds up when a different LLM drives the agents.
- number: accuracy above 0.8 on all four datasets, up to 0.9280 (GT on Mistral 7B).
- setup: a Coding-GD subset re-run with GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek V3, Qwen 7B and Mistral 7B. A separate predictor is trained on each LLM's data, so this is not transfer across LLMs.
- quote: "prediction accuracies of GNNs remain above 0.8 across 4 datasets"
- where: Section 5.3, p.6. Table 4.

5. GNNs beat the alternative predictors on average.
- number: average accuracy GCN 0.8343, MLP 0.7667, fine-tuned Llama 0.7937, untuned DeepSeek V3 0.5323.
- setup: Coding-AF, Math-AF and Reason-AF. The MLP reads raw text. Llama is LoRA-tuned on FLORA-Bench. DeepSeek V3 is prompted zero-shot at temperature 0.
- quote: "DeepSeek-V3, despite its significantly larger parameter volume, fails to achieve accurate predictions compared to GNNs or MLP."
- where: Section 5.6, p.7. Table 9, p.15.
- Tuned Llama wins on Coding-AF (0.8453 against GCN 0.8345). The authors dismiss it as costly to train and run.
- The structure matters: MLP gets 0.7667 against GCN 0.8343 on average, about 7 points.

6. Benchmark facts.
- number: 600k workflow-task pairs, 6 domains, 80/10/10 split.
- setup: workflows are extracted from G-Designer and AFlow runs. They average about 5.5 to 6.6 nodes. Tasks come from HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, MATH and MMLU.
- quote: "The entire benchmark consists of 600k workflow-task pairs and their binary labels denoting success or failure."
- where: Section 1, p.2. Table 1, p.6.
- Workflow counts are small: Coding-AF 38, Math-AF 42, Reason-AF 30, but Coding-GD 739.
- Most samples come from Reason (453,600 and 72,000).

7. Success rate rises with graph size, then saturates and drops.
- number: none beyond the node range 2 to 8.
- quote: "Within the range from 2 to 5, the success rate increases with the number of nodes. However, as the number of nodes continues to increase, the rate of increase in success rate slows down until it saturates, and the success rate even starts to decrease"
- where: Appendix C, p.13. Figure 11, p.14.
- The Figure 11 caption is wrong (a copy of Figure 10's), and no numbers are given.

Method, for a note:
- Each agent is a node whose feature is a sentence-transformer embedding of its system prompt.
- A GNN message-passes over the DAG, then a pooling step produces a graph embedding.
- That embedding is concatenated with a projected task-instruction embedding and fed to an MLP.
- Quote: "g = Pool {h(L)i | vi ∈ V}" (Eq. 8), and "ˆe = MLP(o)" (Eq. 9), p.4.

Metrics:
- Accuracy is the share of correct binary predictions.
- Utility is top-k overlap between the predicted and true workflow rankings (Eq. 11). It is not a rank correlation.

LIMITS
- The authors concede that cross-domain generalization fails and call for new architectures and large-scale pretraining (Section 6).
- It is a position paper with a small experimental base, one run per cell, with no seeds, variance or significance tests.
- Labels come from one LLM (GPT-4o-mini) at temperature 0, with 3 inference runs for stability.
- Workflows are small (about 6 nodes) and come from only two generators, GD and AFlow. AFlow's MCTS caps workflow size, so large topologies are untested.
- The optimization test (RQ4) uses only a GCN, only AFlow, and 3 benchmarks. Time and cost cover the optimization loop only. The one-off cost of building the training labels is not counted.
- The score gap to ground-truth rewards is large on MMLU (0.55 against 0.73).
- Utility metrics are mixed. Reason-GD utility is near chance at 0.59.
- Prompt embeddings are frozen, so the graph structure's contribution is only weakly isolated. The MLP baseline is the only control, and it sees raw text.
- The task filter keeps only tasks with success rates in a middle band (10 to 90 percent in the text; Table 6 uses narrower ranges per dataset). The reported accuracy is on this filtered, balanced set.
- Models used (GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek V3, Llama 3.x) have dated.

BUILDS ON
- Workflow-as-graph optimizers:
  - GPTSwarm (Zhuge et al., cited without year or venue, "Zhuge et al.")
  - G-Designer (Zhang et al., 2024a)
  - AFlow (Zhang et al., 2024b)
  - ADAS (Hu, Lu & Clune, 2024a, arXiv:2408.08435)
  - EvoMAC (Hu et al., 2024b, arXiv:2410.16946)
  - REINFORCE (Williams, 1992)
- GNNs:
  - GCN (Kipf & Welling, 2016)
  - GAT (Velickovic et al., 2017)
  - GraphSAGE (Hamilton et al., 2017)
  - GCNII (Chen et al., 2020, ICML)
  - Graph Transformer (Shi et al., 2020)
  - One For All (Liu & Feng, 2023)
  - Pooling (Xu et al., 2019)
  - GNN benchmarks (Errica et al., 2019; Dwivedi et al., 2023, JMLR; Hu et al., 2020, OGB, NeurIPS)
- The analogy to high-throughput molecule screening (Du et al., 2024, npj Computational Materials; Wu et al., 2023b).
- Datasets: HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU.
- LoRA (Hu et al., 2021).

CODE: None worth keeping. The only code is the toy AFlow `Workflow` class in Figure 4 / Figure 7, which shows how a node's instruction becomes its system prompt.

FIGURES
- Figure 5 (p.8): "GCN as the predictor indeed benefits the optimization of the agentic workflow in terms of both effectiveness and efficiency." It plots time (log scale) against score for ground-truth, random and GCN rewards on HumanEval, MMLU, MBPP and their average. It shows the speed-up against the quality loss in one picture. This is my single candidate, and Table 8 gives the same numbers if a table suits better.
- Figure 2 (p.4), the Flow-GNN architecture, is the alternative if the note needs the pipeline diagram.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- Table 2 anomalies:
  - OFA's Coding-AF numbers (0.8374 and 0.7593) duplicate the OFA Coding-GD row's accuracy and utility.
  - Table 9 gives OFA Coding-AF as 0.8345 and 0.7104.
  - So the OFA Coding-AF cell in Table 2 is probably a copy-paste error.
- Llama is called "3B" in some places and "Llama-3.1-8B" in others.
- Figure 11's caption is wrong.
- Text and Table 6 disagree on the filter thresholds (a flat 10 to 90 percent, against ranges that vary per dataset).
- Reported speed-up (125x) is slightly above the computed ratio (about 122x).
- Do not cite the OFA Coding-AF cell without checking.

FIT
- Best fit is 05-topology-patterns.md, in its section on searching for topologies. The paper's contribution is a cheap surrogate evaluator that replaces LLM runs as the reward when searching workflow graphs with AFlow, G-Designer or GPTSwarm. It also gives the cost trade-off (125x faster, 0.1 score loss).
- Use 13 or 13b only as a short worked example of graph-level regression on a DAG with text-attributed nodes. It adds little on GNN theory, and its negative finding (no cross-domain transfer) is the main lesson for a representation-learning chapter.
- I could not check which of 13 and 13b exists, or what they say, so choose between them yourself.
